findings.title: Login-list invalidation uses an organization-aware original model
findings.body: `original` is obtained through `getById()` in `update()`, which wraps organization-linked providers so that `isEnabled()` is false whenever their organization is disabled. The updated model is normally the raw model, however. Consequently, while an organization is disabled, changing a previously public/enabled provider to hidden, link-only, disabled, or non-public makes both predicates false and this early return leaves the login list cached. When the organization is enabled again, that cached list still contains the provider and `getForLogin()` does not reapply the hide/link/public predicate while resolving cached IDs, so the provider can be returned/displayed despite no longer qualifying. Determine eligibility from the persisted/raw original model (for example, load it from the delegate) rather than the organization-aware wrapper before deciding whether to invalidate.

findings.title: New test cleanup registrations remove a nonexistent literal alias
findings.body: Each provider created in the loop registers cleanup for `identityProviders().get("alias")` rather than for the generated `idp-alias-<n>` alias; the same mistake is repeated for `idp-alias-20` at line 425. The cleanup therefore does not remove the providers created by this test, which can leave test data behind and contaminate subsequent tests or cause cleanup failures. Register cleanup using the actual alias for each created representation.
